headlines.title: ConocoPhillips’ 2.3% Yield Is Just the Start of the Story
headlines.summary: ConocoPhillips (NYSE:COP) is more than just a play on oil prices. With a huge resource base, a strong foothold in the Permian Basin, and a global mix of exploration and production assets, the company has the scale to keep cash flowing, even as markets shift.

headlines.title: How Buy Ratings Could Impact ConocoPhillips Stock
headlines.summary: ConocoPhillips recently drew attention after analysts highlighted its solid fundamentals, including a forward P/E of 12.5x and meaningful free cash flow that supports both reinvestment and shareholder distributions. Beyond the valuation headline, the long run revenue growth profile and scale driven market share position ConocoPhillips as a large exploration and production operator with significant operational heft.

headlines.title: Wall Street Analysts Think ConocoPhillips (COP) Is a Good Investment: Is It?
headlines.summary: The average brokerage recommendation (ABR) for ConocoPhillips (COP) is equivalent to a Buy. The overly optimistic recommendations of Wall Street analysts make the effectiveness of this highly sought-after metric questionable. So, is it worth buying the stock?

description: ConocoPhillips explores for, produces, transports, and markets crude oil, bitumen, natural gas, liquefied natural gas (LNG), and natural gas liquids. It operates in five segments: Alaska; Lower 48; Canada; Europe, Middle East and North Africa; and Asia Pacific. The company's portfolio includes unconventional plays in North America; conventional assets in North America, Europe, Asia, and Australia; global LNG developments; oil sands assets in Canada; and an inventory of global exploration prospects. It serves in the United States, Canada, China, Equatorial Guinea, Libya, Malaysia, Norway, Singapore, the United Kingdom, and internationally. ConocoPhillips was founded in 1917 and is headquartered in Houston, Texas.
